title: Who may ask
description: The gate in front of every route, pairing, the local token and the device list. A port of the Swift app's RemoteAuth and RemoteServer: the bodies, the sentences and the cookie are the ones its page (net/fetch.js, door/door.js) already reads, which is why a refusal here is the Swift envelope `{"error":{"code","message","request_id"}}` rather than this daemon's flat Refusal. Open without a token: the page, its bundle (/app/, /assets/, /strings/), the icons, /v1/health, /v1/strings and /v1/auth/*. Everything else needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or the `clawdline-next` cookie. Anything but GET and HEAD is a change, and the gate asks three more things of it: an Origin, when there is one, is this request's own (scheme, host and port); a change carried by the cookie has an Origin, and a Sec-Fetch-Site of same-origin when it has one; and its body is application/json or nothing at all, else 415 unsupported_media_type. The cookie is not called `clawdline`, as the Swift app's is, because a browser does not separate cookies by port: one name on 127.0.0.1 would make each app sign the other out.

AuthError.description: The inside of every refusal the gate and the auth routes give. `code` is the part a client may branch on; `message` is English, for a person.

code.description: unauthorized, forbidden, wrong_code, expired, rate_limited, bad_request, not_found, store_unavailable, unsupported_media_type.

request_id.description: A fresh lowercase UUID per refusal, for finding it in a log.

tries_left.description: Only on wrong_code: how many guesses pairing has left, so a page need not count for itself. The count is across pairings, not per pairing: asking again does not refill it.

PairRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/pair. Open without a token. Three in ten minutes, then 429 rate_limited; also 429 rate_limited while five wrong codes in the last day keep pairing closed.

name.description: What to call the device; trimmed, at most forty characters, `A browser` when empty.

PairStarted.description: The answer to a pairing request. The six-digit code is never in it: it is shown on this machine, to a local-token holder, and typed into the device.

expires.description: Unix seconds. Two minutes after the request.

PairConfirm.description: POST /v1/auth/pair/confirm. A wrong code is 403 wrong_code with tries_left. Five wrong codes in a day, whichever pairings they were typed into, close pairing: the fifth, and every confirmation after it, is 403 expired, as are a lapsed pairing and a replaced one.

AdoptRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/adopt: a token the page was handed in a URL fragment, traded for the cookie EventSource needs. Nothing is granted: an unknown token is 401.

PasswordRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/password: a correct password mints a new read-only device. Ten wrong passwords in a day, from everybody together, and the checks still under way count toward the same ten; past it, 429 rate_limited before any hashing. `name` is cut to forty characters before it is stored or audited.

SignedIn.description: A new or adopted token, twice: here for a script, and in `Set-Cookie: clawdline-next=…; Path=/; Max-Age=31536000; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` (plus `; Secure` behind an HTTPS proxy) for a page.

AuthOK.description: POST /v1/auth/logout, and the device routes that only change something.

caps.description: read, and send when this device may type into a session.

last_seen.description: Unix seconds of the last request it made since the daemon started or last saved; absent when never.

DeviceList.description: GET /v1/auth/devices. This machine's own token only; a paired device is refused.

configured.description: Whether a person has paired something or set a password — the tunnel interlock's question. This machine's own token does not count.

CapsRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/devices/{id}/caps. read is always kept; send is the only other grant. Local token only.

RevokedAll.description: POST /v1/auth/devices/revoke-all: every paired device, the password and the open pairing. This machine's own token stays.

BrowserRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/devices/browser: `clawdline open` asking for a device of its own. Local token only.

send.description: Also grant send. Off unless the person at this machine asked.

BrowserDevice.description: A device minted for a browser on this machine. `url` carries the token in its fragment, which a browser never sends and never logs; the page trades it for the cookie with /v1/auth/adopt.

PasswordSet.description: POST /v1/auth/devices/password. Empty clears it. Local token only.

PairingNotice.description: One `pairing` event on GET /v1/auth/pairings, the server-sent stream only this machine's own token may open. It is the one place the code leaves the daemon. The stream starts with the pairing open now, if any.
